SUBJECT: SUPERMARKET RAPID FACT REPORT

Attached please find the latest Supermarket Rapid Fact Report for the week ending 5/17/92. This service provides weekly information (share, coupon availability, coupon values and carton pricing) based on scanning supermarkets across the Total U.S.

KEY FINDINGS

- Marlboro's share remained stable at \(20.1\%\) on a one and four week basis in the absence of any supermarket specific promotional activities.

- Retail prices have not yet stabilized following the early April manufacturer price change announcements with Marlboro, Branded Generic and Sub Generic carton prices advancing by +4.9% (80¢), +6.6% (96¢), and +8.1% (94¢) respectively from end of March levels.

- The retail price difference between Black & Whites and Sub-Generics has widened from 81¢ per carton on 3/29 to $1.88 this week, while the difference between Marlboro and B&W's has expanded from $5.62 (34%) per carton to $6.55 (38%). In contrast, the price difference between Marlboro and Branded Generics narrowed from $2.03 to $1.86 per carton in the last six weeks.

- Although Brown & Williamson did not increase the manufacturers list price of Raleigh Extra in April, its retail price per carton has increased +7.3% or $0.82 since the end of March.

- The Discount Category advanced +0.3 share points versus week-ago, with advances by the Branded (+0.4) and Sub Generic (+0.1) segments partially offset by declining B&W/PL performance (-0.2).

- Doral posted a +0.3 point gain versus week-ago and its latest four week share is +0.8 points ahead of 13 week-ago, reflecting its shift back to more aggressive coupon support. For the second consecutive week, Doral $5.00 IRC's were evident in 20% of supermarkets, while in contrast, Cambridge and Viceroy $5.00 levels only reached 12% each this week.

EMERGING TRENDS

- Doral $5.50 IRC activity was evident for the third consecutive week, with availability in 1% of stores this week, and $6.00 values were noted for the first time this week (1% of stores).

- While Bristol's IRC support at the $3.00 level has declined from 4% to 2% in the last four weeks, its major Sub Generic competitors have doubled their $3.00 offers. Specifically, Raleigh Extra, Magna, and Sterling now provide $3.00 IRC's in 6%, 13%, and 16% of stores respectively.

• True significantly increased its $3.00 couponing, doubling from 13% of stores last week to 26% this week while reducing its $2.00, $4.00 and $6.00 offers.
